title: How to start homeschooling: first-month paperwork
dek: Sort your legal start conditions, withdrawal, school records and first teaching log before buying a full system for your new homeschool.
metaDescription: Sort your legal start conditions, withdrawal, school records and first teaching log before buying a full system for your new homeschool.

paragraphs: Start homeschooling by confirming the legal route and start conditions for your child, completing required filings in the correct order, documenting withdrawal if enrolled, and keeping an actual instruction record from the start. Do not assume withdrawal always comes before notice or acknowledgement.

When the decision has been made, the temptation is to order everything at once: books, planner, printer and folders. The paperwork has a smaller job. It should make the transition traceable and prevent a missed obligation while you work out how teaching will look. This US guide focuses on that first month, not curriculum selection or a guarantee of legal compliance.

body.heading: Build the transition file
items: Write down your state, child's age, present enrollment and chosen education route. Confirm which authority handles that route.
Read its official start requirements, including subjects, instructional time, notice, qualifications and assessment obligations where applicable.
Confirm what must happen before withdrawal. Save any required acknowledgement and the school's withdrawal confirmation with their actual dates.
Request useful existing records through the school's accepted process: report cards, transcript, assessments and relevant support or health documents.
Create one place for submissions and another for actual learning evidence. Start with dated entries rather than a blank annual portfolio.
List each confirmed future obligation with its trigger, due date, recipient and evidence needed. Do not rely on a generic school-year calendar.

body.heading: The order must fit your state
paragraphs: [North Carolina's official guidance](https://www.doa.nc.gov/divisions/non-public-education/home-schools/faqs/opening-closing-reopening) instructs families to continue current attendance until the registration process is complete. That is why a national checklist cannot safely say "withdraw, then file." Other routes differ. Ask the specific sequence question before agreeing a final attendance date.

Use the school's accepted withdrawal and records-request channels. That may be a portal, form, email or letter, not necessarily two hand-delivered letters. Withdrawal and a records request do different jobs even when one message addresses both. Retain evidence that each request was received.

body.heading: First-month milestones, not universal deadlines
rows: Check any required acknowledgement or approval.
Clarify anything outstanding with the school.
Resolve unknown obligations rather than assuming none.

body.heading: Example: a workable first file
paragraphs: Invented example: Morgan is moving a nine-year-old from school to parent-directed home education. Morgan creates a folder called Transition, saves the official instructions and submits the required registration. Only after confirming the permitted sequence does Morgan finalize withdrawal. A records request asks for the last report, assessment information and existing support documents.

The first learning entry is specific: November 18, fractions, compared halves and quarters using paper shapes; explained equivalence with prompting. It is evidence of that activity, not a claim that every subject or requirement has been satisfied. The family adds other mandated subjects and starts the relevant attendance measure immediately.

body.heading: Do not postpone support arrangements
paragraphs: If your child has an IEP, disability-related services or an evaluation underway, ask how changing education routes affects those arrangements before withdrawing. Do not assume services transfer unchanged or automatically disappear. Keep the current documents and the contact for the responsible office.

If a custody order or agreement governs education decisions, resolve the authority question before changing enrollment. If you receive an attendance warning or a filing rejection, seek state-specific legal or administrative help promptly. A later portfolio cannot by itself repair an unmet start condition.

items.line: Please confirm the withdrawal process and send the available report cards, assessments and relevant support records. Which request channel should I use, and how will I know it has been received?
For this legal route and my child's age, what record or assessment is required after we start? Please point me to the current published instructions and the date trigger.

body.heading: Keep the first system deliberately small
paragraphs: Use a folder, notebook or spreadsheet you can open after a busy teaching day. Record actual work, not just planned lessons. Where required, keep the appropriate time or day measure alongside it. [Multiple-child record keeping](/guides/homeschool-record-keeping-for-multiple-children) explains how to avoid mixing siblings' evidence.

An adjustment period may be useful for your family, but there is no universal month-per-year deschooling formula. A lighter routine still needs to meet applicable duties. Buy materials when you can identify the need they serve, rather than using purchases as proof that the transition is complete.

items.a: Only if the applicable start conditions are met. Check the route, age rules, required filings and withdrawal sequence first. If acknowledgement or another condition is outstanding, do not assume a planned start date overrides it. Ask the responsible office how to handle an urgent transition.

items.q: Do I need a complete curriculum before the first day?
items.a: You need a workable way to provide whatever instruction your route requires. That is not necessarily a large boxed curriculum. Check mandated subjects and your child's needs, choose appropriate materials, and record what happens. A notebook alone is an organizing tool, not an education program.

items.q: What if the school records have not arrived?
items.a: Keep the request receipt and follow up through the school's published process. Ask which records are available and who handles the request rather than inventing a national response deadline. Work from the information you have while avoiding guesses about past achievement or support arrangements.

research.intent: Order first-month administration around local start conditions, without prescribing curriculum or a universal withdrawal sequence.

sourceChecks.verified: Current official search text: continue attendance until registration is complete; one notice per household, not annually or per child.

limitations: One official state counterexample verifies why the sequence must be conditional. This is not a comprehensive state law checklist.
Saved search leads were reviewed for reader language only, not authority or prevalence. Quora was blocked in saved research. No search-volume or ranking estimate is available.
